title: Looking back: kingdom and loss
hookLine: Ranjit Singh's Punjab, the wars and the exiles

cards: Gold on a temple roof in Amritsar, catching the morning light. A great diamond, wrapped and carried away across the sea. A mother, sent away from her young son.

A boy, growing up among strangers, far from Punjab. The son of a misl chief became a Maharaja, built a kingdom, and covered the Harmandir in gold. After his death, almost everything he built was lost.

teach.b: First, the kingdom. Ranjit Singh rose from the Sukerchakia misl, entered Lahore, and was crowned Maharaja.

He called his government the Sarkar-e-Khalsa, the Khalsa's government, and struck coins in the Gurus' names, not his own. He trained a modern army and covered the Harmandir in gilded copper and marble.
In English, it came to be called the Golden Temple.
Second, the wars. After his death came quarrels at court, then wars with the British. At Sobraon the Sikh army was defeated, and Sikh memory holds that some of its own commanders betrayed it.
At Chillianwala it held its ground. At Gujrat it lost, and Punjab was annexed. Third, the exiles.
Maharani Jind Kaur was separated from her son and sent away.

teach.h: THE EXILES: A QUEEN, A DIAMOND, A BOY.
teach.b: The Koh-i-Noor diamond was taken from the boy king, Duleep Singh, and sent to Queen Victoria. He was raised by British guardians, far from home, and baptized a Christian.
Fourth, what was kept. The kingdom ended, but the Harmandir still shines. The Granth was still read, the Ardas still said, the langar still served.
And the boy, grown up, went looking for the faith he'd been taken from. A kingdom can be signed away on paper. A faith, it turned out, was harder to take.

how: Sikhs remember Maharaja Ranjit Singh's rule and the fall of the Sikh kingdom in histories, songs and gatherings; the gilded Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar remains a living center of Sikh worship.

games.q: you are Duleep Singh: a king as a boy, raised far away by guardians, baptized in another faith. you are grown now. what do you do?
o: go looking for the faith you were taken from.
ask for the diamond back and nothing else.
games.why: as a grown man he sought to return to the Sikh faith: a kingdom was lost, but the faith was harder to take.

practice: On one side, let something you've lost come to mind, a place, a person, a role, a time of life, and just let it be named. On the other side, look for what you kept through that loss: a habit, a love, a word, a way of being.
Hold both, one in each hand, and if you pray, say Waheguru over each one.

wordCard.voice: Looking back. Today at Ranjit Singh's Punjab, the wars with the British, the exiles of a queen, a diamond and a boy, and what survived the end of the kingdom. Today's word.
